query: The Book Behind the Counter {Behind Mr Grimsby's counter there's a book wrapped in brown paper, kept apart. "For someone who'll need it," he says vaguely. "Not you. Or not yet."|The wrapped book is still there. Mr Grimsby moves it a little further from you when you come in.|The brown-paper book has a name pencilled on it now, but he keeps his thumb over the name.} Wait to be the someone {You browse for an hour in plain sight, being the sort of person who'd need a book. Mr Grimsby sells you a history of lighthouses instead.|You come back twice in the week. On the second visit he lets you hold it, then takes it back. "Soon," he says.|You don't ask. Mr Grimsby notices you not asking, and approves, and doesn't give you the book.} Buy what he recommends instead {He hands you something about tides that smells of seaweed. Chapter two is exactly what your essay needed, as usual, annoyingly.|You buy his recommendation without arguing. He looks almost disappointed you didn't fight for the other one.|A slim book on candle-making, for reasons he won't explain. You'll need it on Thursday.} Charm the parcel out of him {You smile at him with a little more charm than you own, and he finds himself handing you the parcel. "Ah," he says, puzzled. "It was you all along. Was it?"|Glamour, and a compliment about his shelving. He unwraps the book for you himself. It's the one you came in for last month and couldn't find.|He beams, decides you've been a customer for years, and wraps the parcel again for you, more nicely, with string.}

results.title: Out of Print
results.excerpt:
Out of Print
You need a book for an essay: the one every reading list cites and nobody has seen in thirty years. The library's copy went missing before you arrived. Grimsby, asked, gives you a book about lighthouses instead and says it's the next best thing. He may even be right.
